entries.title: II Corinthians 12:1
segments: I must needs glory. The attitude of the Corinthians toward Paul's accuser forced him to recount to them circumstances which would tend to prove his devotion to the cause of Christ.  But even this he did under protest.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:2
segments: Fourteen years ago. The vision on the road to Damascus (
) had occurred about twenty years before; and it is generally believed that the vision here referred to is that in the Temple, recorded in

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:4
segments: Paradise. The word is used to signify the heavenly abode of departed spirits.  See

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:6
segments: For I shall speak the truth. The inference is that Paul's accuser was not careful to restrict his boasting to simple fact.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:7
segments: A thorn in the flesh. There have been many conjectures as to the nature of this affliction.  Paul's reference to it suggests that it was a source of constant humiliation, lest he be consumed with pride.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:9
segments: My grace is sufficient for thee. From this it would seem that the desired healing was denied to Paul, and that it was shown him that the grace of God manifest in him was wholly sufficient to overbalance any physical deficiency.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:10
segments: For when I am weak, then am I strong. His weakness led him the more quickly and earnestly to seek the power of Christ.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:11
segments: Though I am nothing. All glory belongs to Christ.  See

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:12
segments: By signs and wonders.  See note on

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:14
segments: But the parents for the children. Paul stood in the place of father to the church in Corinth (
).  This relation ought to be a sufficient answer to his critics.  See

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:18
segments: Did Titus take any advantage of you? Whether a similar charge had been made against Titus or not, Paul answers it.

entries.title: II Corinthians 12:21
segments: Should humble me before you. Through the relapsing into sinful ways, without repentance, of some of Paul's converts.  This was also doubtless intended as a rebuke and warning to those who had thus fallen away.
